Belarus Grapples with Major Cyber Attack Disrupting Power and Payments

MINSK – A wide-scale cyber attack targeting Belarus’s national power grid and electronic payments networks forced businesses and households across the country into disruption on Tuesday, as authorities scrambled to assess the damage and restore services.

The State Energy Coordination Board confirmed that several regional substations and control centers had been compromised early in the morning, resulting in rolling blackouts in Minsk, Gomel, and Brest. At the same time, major payment processors, including BelPay and the Unified National Payments Center, reported technical outages that left thousands of merchants unable to process card transactions.

“Engineers are working around the clock to limit the impact and restore electricity as swiftly as possible,” said Deputy Energy Minister Ivan Gusev at a midday press conference. “We urge citizens to conserve power and avoid unnecessary travel.”

Supermarket chains reported difficulties with refrigeration and inventory management, while banks limited withdrawals and warned customers of possible delays in salary payments. “We have backup systems in place, but the extent of the disruption is unprecedented,” said Dina Moroz, spokesperson for the Belarusian Retailers Association.

The Belarusian Union of Industrialists and Entrepreneurs estimated that factory stoppages and shipment delays could cost businesses up to $45 million per day if the outages persist. Telecommunications services, while largely operational, experienced intermittent slowdowns.

Cybersecurity analysts say the breadth of the attack suggests careful planning. “This is a coordinated assault on critical infrastructure, aimed at maximum economic disruption,” said Kirill Savitsky, head of research at Minsk Cyber Defense Institute.

Authorities have not attributed blame and have cautioned against speculation as investigations continue. No timeline for full restoration has been provided.
